Artificial intelligence has the potential to be an incredible tool for good in our world. In fact, we’ve already seen its potential in numerous professional fields, such as business, economics, medicine, science, and–near and dear to my heart–meteorology. But even with this great potential for good, we are faced with equally incredible danger. AI models have shown the capacity to conduct increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, both when weaponized by bad actors and even, in particularly frightening cases, of their own accord, and it is critical we work to enact the proper safeguards before it’s too late.

It is also important that we maintain our technological superiority over China so we can ensure Americans’ private data, crucial digital infrastructure systems, and our national security interests continue to be protected. [...] If we want to win the AI race with China, we need to enable innovation in the domestic artificial intelligence market, and comprehensive regulation lets us do just that.

We must provide clear and comprehensive national regulations to help create a level playing field for newcomers, minimize catastrophic risk, protect vulnerable populations from the misuse of the technology, and eliminate any legal ambiguities.
